description: Removals of Native nations, one entry per stage: where each nation was moved from, where it was sent, the years, the legal basis and a quotation from the treaty, statute or official source naming the destination. Compiled Nov. 27, 2026 by two research subagents and checked by the thread session (quotes from HTML sources re-matched by script against the fetched pages; Statutes at Large quotes re-matched against the volumes' text). Review status: Unverified.

from.description: Cherokee towns in Georgia, Alabama and Tennessee; lands ceded in exchange for land for emigrants on the Arkansas

to.description: Between the Arkansas and White rivers, Arkansas Territory (later moved by 1828 treaty)
to.notes_place: Arkansas River (Q8319) is a river or territory, not a point; placed by its land instead
to.place_note: Placed by the thread session from this stage's own description (the Arkansas Cherokee lands between the Arkansas and White rivers; county chosen as an anchor, from memory)

removals.quote: to give to that part of the Cherokee nation on the Arkansas as much land on said river and White river as they have or may hereafter receive from the Cherokee nation east of the Mississippi, acre for acre

sources.what: Cherokee treaty of Feb. 27, 1819; annuity split between East and West Cherokees

removals.notes: Voluntary emigration treaties. Royce values taken from cessions dated 1817-07-08 and 1819-02-27 whose project treaty ids match. The 1819 treaty names Cherokees "west of the Mississippi" but no destination article was quoted. To-place is the Arkansas River as a regional anchor.

from.description: Cherokee settlements in Arkansas Territory on the Arkansas and White rivers
from.place_note: Placed by the thread session from this stage's own description (same anchor as cherokee-1817)

to.description: Seven million acres west of Arkansas and Missouri, later northeastern Oklahoma (Cherokee Nation)

removals.quote: The United States agree to possess the Cherokees, and to guarantee it to them forever, and that guarantee is hereby solemnly pledged, of seven millions of acres of land

sources.what: Treaty with the Western Cherokee, May 6, 1828
Supplementary treaty Feb. 14, 1833 fixing the boundaries

removals.notes: Royce 489 and 492 are the Oklahoma tracts listed under the 1833 treaty; confirm they are the 1828 grant. 1833 article field left blank.

from.description: Cherokee Nation in Georgia, North Carolina, Tennessee and Alabama; gathered in army stockades 1838

to.description: Cherokee Nation west of Arkansas and Missouri (northeastern Oklahoma)

legal_basis.statute: Act of May 28, 1830 (Indian Removal Act), ch. 148

removals.quote: The Cherokee nation hereby cede relinquish and convey to the United States all the lands owned claimed or possessed by them east of the Mississippi river

sources.what: NPS: New Echota treaty and the 1838 roundup by federal troops and state militias

removals.notes: Quote names the cession, not the destination; the destination is in art. 2 (lands guaranteed by the 1828 and 1833 treaties plus an additional tract). Removal executed by the U.S. Army in 1838 after Senate ratification (1836); the Act of 1830 is cited as general authority, not quoted. The treaty was signed by a minority faction.

from.description: Choctaw lands in Mississippi (Treaty of Doak's Stand cession)

to.description: Tract between the Arkansas and Red rivers in Arkansas Territory (later reduced by the 1825 treaty)
to.notes_place: Arkansas River (Q8319) is a river or territory, not a point; placed by its land instead

removals.quote: do hereby cede to said nation, a tract of country west of the Mississippi River, situate between the Arkansas and Red River

sources.what: Treaty of Jan. 20, 1825 revising the western boundary

removals.notes: Few Choctaws moved under this treaty; most removal was under the 1830 treaty. Royce 122 is the Arkansas tract listed for 1820 and 1825.

from.description: Choctaw Nation lands in Mississippi and Alabama (Dancing Rabbit Creek)

to.description: Choctaw Nation, beginning near Fort Smith, Arkansas (southeastern Oklahoma)
to.place_note: Fort Smith (Q79535), named by the subagent, is the border crossing, not the Choctaw land; placed by the Census area instead

legal_basis.statute: Act of May 28, 1830 (Indian Removal Act), ch. 148

removals.quote: a tract of country west of the Mississippi River, in fee simple to them and their descendants, to inure to them while they shall exist as a nation and live on it, beginning near Fort Smith

sources.what: Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek, Sept. 27, 1830

removals.notes: Removal carried out in waves 1831, 1832, 1833 under War Department supervision. Place is Fort Smith because the grant begins "near Fort Smith". Mississippi Band of Choctaw (those who stayed) not linked.

from.description: Chickasaw Nation lands in northern Mississippi and Alabama, ceded 1832; Pontotoc

to.description: Chickasaw District of the Choctaw Nation, south-central Oklahoma, agreed at Doaksville near Fort Towson

removals.quote: the Chickasaws shall have the privilege of forming a district within the limits of their country
removals.notes: The 1832 and 1834 treaties only promise a search for a western home; the first destination named is the Choctaw country in 1837. The 1837 convention is cited as 11 Stat. 573 in the project data. Removal 1837-1838. The Oct. 22, 1832 treaty (7 Stat. 388) is also relevant.

from.description: Creek lands in Georgia (Treaty of Indian Springs, annulled 1826; emigration agreed by the Treaty of Washington 1826)

to.description: Arkansas River at the mouth of the Canadian fork, west of the Mississippi
to.notes_place: Arkansas River (Q8319) is a river or territory, not a point; placed by its land instead

removals.quote: the like quantity, acre for acre, westward of the Mississippi, on the Arkansas river, commencing at the mouth of the Canadian Fork thereof
removals.notes: The 1825 treaty was repudiated and replaced by the 1826 treaty, which kept the offer to the McIntosh party to remove. Royce numbers are from the 1826 cession. Migration largely 1827-1828.

from.description: Creek Nation lands in eastern Alabama ceded at Cusseta

to.description: Creek country west of the Mississippi, central eastern Oklahoma (Canadian and Arkansas rivers area), boundaries set by the 1833 treaty

removals.quote: The United States are desirous that the Creeks should remove to the country west of the Mississippi, and join their countrymen there

sources.what: Treaty of Feb. 14, 1833 defining the Creek country in the west
Background on Creek forced removal 1836-37 after the Creek War of 1836

removals.notes: The treaty says no Creek is compelled to emigrate; mass removal came 1836-1837 under army control after the 1836 hostilities (military kind assigned for that reason). Tribal towns listed are descendants of Creek towns; mapping approximate.

from.description: Seminole lands in Florida Territory (Payne's Landing)

to.description: Creek country west of the Mississippi; Seminole tract between the Canadian and its north fork assigned at Fort Gibson 1833

removals.quote: agree to emigrate to the country assigned to the Creeks, west of the Mississippi river

sources.what: Second Seminole War 1835-42, army enforcement of removal

removals.notes: Seminole leaders disputed the treaty; removal was enforced during the Second Seminole War 1835-1842. Place is Fort Gibson (treaty site) as a regional anchor, not the actual settlement. Seminoles lived within the Creek Nation until 1856.

from.description: Creek Nation in Indian Territory, where the Seminoles had been settled under the 1845 treaty
from.notes_place: Indian Territory (Q868245) is a river or territory, not a point; placed by its land instead

to.description: Own tract between the Canadian and its North Fork west of the 97th parallel (Indian Territory)
to.notes_place: Canadian River (Q597753) is a river or territory, not a point; placed by its land instead

removals.quote: The Creek Nation doth hereby grant, cede, and convey to the Seminole Indians, the tract of country
removals.notes: Not a forced removal but a relocation to a separate Seminole domain. Royce 480 is the Oklahoma tract listed under the 1856 treaty (not verified as the Seminole grant). 1845 treaty article left blank.

from.description: Seminole tract ceded by the Creek Nation in 1856 (west-central Indian Territory)

to.description: New Seminole reservation on former Creek lands (present Seminole County, Oklahoma)

removals.quote: the Seminoles cede and convey to the United States their entire domain
removals.notes: Post-Civil-War cession and relocation. Quote names the cession; the new reservation is described in the same treaty. Royce numbers may be empty if the treaty id does not match.

from.description: Seminole remnant in southern Florida after the Third Seminole War
from.place_note: Placed by the thread session from this stage's own description (from memory: the 1858 emigrants left from Fort Myers; check)

to.description: Seminole country in Indian Territory (1856 tract)
to.notes_place: Indian Territory (Q868245) is a river or territory, not a point; placed by its land instead

removals.quote: The United States agree to remove comfortably to their new country west, all those Seminoles now in Florida who can be induced to emigrate thereto

sources.what: Treaty of Aug. 7, 1856, article on emigration of Florida Seminoles
Third Seminole War ended 1858 with the emigration of Billy Bowlegs and his band

removals.notes: Emigration was induced by payment at the end of the Third Seminole War; the treaty authority is the 1856 agreement. The Seminole Tribe of Florida descends from those who stayed.

from.description: Apalachicola band reservation on the Apalachicola River, Florida

to.description: "Country west" in search of a home; the 1833 treaty names the country allotted to the Creeks and Seminoles (exact place undetermined)

removals.quote: to meet the charges of a party to explore immediately the country west in search of a home more suitable to their habits
removals.notes: Present-day successor nation not identified (apalachicola-band-of-creek-indians and the-apalachicola-river-community exist in the project but are not established descendants of emigrants). Destination is not fixed by the treaty.

removals.people: United Nation of Chippewa, Ottawa and Potawatomi (Treaty of Chicago)

from.description: Lands along the western shore of Lake Michigan in Illinois and Wisconsin

to.description: Tract of not less than five million acres on the Missouri River beginning at the mouth of the Boyer River (Iowa; Council Bluffs)

removals.quote: a tract of country west of the Mississippi river, to be assigned to them by the President of the United States—to be not less in quantity than five millions of acres
removals.notes: Many Michigan and Wisconsin bands did not remove (e.g. Pokagon, Forest County). Royce 265 is the Iowa tract. Nations listed are those that ended up in Kansas/Oklahoma; other successor bands omitted.

removals.people: Potawatomi of Indiana (Tippecanoe, Yellow River and Wabash bands)

from.description: Reservations in northern Indiana created by the 1832 Tippecanoe treaties

to.description: Country provided for the Potawatomi west of the Mississippi (Osage River sub-agency, eastern Kansas)

removals.quote: to remove to the country provided for the Pottawatamy nation west of the Mississippi river within two years

sources.what: Treaty of Mar. 29, 1836 (typical of the series)

removals.notes: Series of small 1836-37 treaties each ceding a reserve and requiring removal within two years. The treaties name only "the country west of the Mississippi"; the Kansas location (Osage River, Osawatomie) is from later history, not these texts. Article numbers left blank where a treaty has no numbered articles. Royce list is the Indiana cessions dated on those treaty dates.

removals.people: Potawatomi (Chief Menominee's band, Trail of Death)

from.description: Menominee Reserve at Twin Lakes near Plymouth, Indiana

to.description: Osage River sub-agency near Osawatomie, Kansas (Potawatomi reserve)

removals.quote: agree to remove to the country west of the Mississippi river, provided for the Potawattimie nation by the United States within two years

sources.what: Forced march by Indiana militia, Sept.-Nov. 1838, Twin Lakes to Osawatomie
Kansas Historical Society: Menominee refused to sign the Yellow River treaty; Gov. Wallace authorized Gen. Tipton's militia

removals.notes: Chief Menominee refused to sign the Aug. 5, 1836 treaty; removal was by Indiana militia under Gen. John Tipton, authorised by Gov. David Wallace. Legal basis is the Aug. 5, 1836 treaty and the Feb. 11, 1837 assent treaty.

from.description: Potawatomi lands at Council Bluffs, Iowa Territory

to.description: 576,000-acre tract on the Kansas River, Kansas
to.notes_place: Kansas River (Q1367638) is a river or territory, not a point; placed by its land instead

removals.quote: The said tribes of Indians agree to remove to their new homes on the Kansas River, within two years from the ratification of this treaty
removals.notes: Royce 433/434 are the Kansas Potawatomi reservation tracts listed under the 1846 and 1861 treaties.

from.description: Potawatomi reservation on the Kansas River

to.description: Reservation in the Indian country south of Kansas (central Oklahoma)

removals.quote: a home should be secured for them in the Indian country south of Kansas
removals.notes: Quote is the treaty recital; the operative article provides for selecting the reservation. Actual move in the 1870s. The Prairie Band remained in Kansas. Royce 506 is the Oklahoma tract listed under the 1867 treaty. Pottawatomie County anchor is approximate.

from.description: Winnebago lands in Wisconsin and Illinois, ceded in 1832 and 1837

to.description: The Neutral Ground west of the Mississippi in northeastern Iowa

removals.quote: The said Indians agree to remove within eight months from the ratification of this treaty, to that portion of the neutral ground west of the Mississippi
removals.notes: The Neutral Ground grant is in the 1832 treaty; most Winnebago left only after the 1840 military removal by U.S. Dragoons (not separately sourced here). Many returned to Wisconsin. Winneshiek County is a regional anchor for the Neutral Ground. Royce 267 spans IA and MN.

from.description: Neutral Ground, Iowa

to.description: Reservation near Long Prairie, Minnesota Territory

removals.quote: a tract of country north of St. Peter’s and west of the Mississippi Rivers, of not less than eight hundred thousand acres
removals.notes: Treaty names only a tract north of St. Peter's River and west of the Mississippi; Long Prairie is the site chosen in 1847. Removal 1848.

from.description: Long Prairie reservation, Minnesota

to.description: Blue Earth reservation, Minnesota
to.notes_place: Blue Earth River (Q885697) is a river or territory, not a point; placed by its land instead

removals.quote: a tract of land equal to eighteen miles square, on the Blue Earth River, in the Territory of Minnesota
removals.notes: West-of-Mississippi stage included to complete the journey. Later stages (Crow Creek 1863, Nebraska 1865 treaty, 14 Stat. 671) not covered.

from.description: Saukenuk and Rock River country, Illinois (ceded by the 1804 treaty)

to.description: West side of the Mississippi in Iowa (no specific place)

removals.quote: As long as the lands which are now ceded to the United States remain their property, the Indians belonging to the said tribes, shall enjoy the privilege of living and hunting upon them

sources.what: Treaty of St. Louis, Nov. 3, 1804, art. 7
Context: Sauk expelled from Saukenuk in 1831 by militia and army, leading to the 1832 war

removals.notes: Weak legal case: art. 7 allowed living on the ceded lands only while they remained U.S. property; after the lands were sold (1829-30) the army and Illinois militia expelled the Sauk (June 1831). The destination is not in the treaty. Royce 50 spans IL, MO and WI.

from.description: Sauk and Fox lands in Iowa Territory ceded in 1842

to.description: Tract on the Missouri River or its waters; in practice the Osage River reservation in eastern Kansas

removals.quote: which tract of land shall be upon the Missouri river, or some of its waters
removals.notes: Treaty text says "upon the Missouri river, or some of its waters"; the actual reserve (Osage River, Franklin County, Kansas, 1845) is from history rather than the treaty. Meskwaki later returned to Iowa by purchase in 1856-57 (not sourced here). Source lands are west of the Mississippi.

removals.people: Sauk and Fox of the Mississippi

from.description: Sac and Fox reservation in Osage and Franklin counties, Kansas

to.description: Indian country south of Kansas and south of the Cherokee lands, central Oklahoma

removals.quote: a tract of land in the Indian country south of Kansas, and south of the Cherokee lands, not exceeding seven hundred and fifty square miles in extent
removals.notes: Royce 495 is the Oklahoma tract listed under this treaty.

from.description: Kickapoo lands in Illinois and Indiana

to.description: Tract on the Osage River (Pommes de Terre), Missouri
to.place_note: Royce 179 is the Missouri land granted to the Kickapoo in 1819-1820 and ceded in 1832 (land-cessions.json)

removals.quote: a certain tract of land lying in the territory of Missouri
removals.notes: Quote names Missouri Territory; the boundary description (confluence of Pommes de Terre and Osage) is in the same article. No Wikidata place chosen.

from.description: Kickapoo lands on the Osage River, Missouri

to.description: Country on the Missouri River north of the Delaware lands (Leavenworth and Atchison area, Kansas)

removals.quote: from the country ceded on Osage river, in the State of Missouri, to the country selected on the Missouri river, north of lands which have been assigned to the Delawares
removals.notes: The Kansas Kickapoo Reservation (Brown County) came later (1854 treaty); Oklahoma Kickapoo moved from Kansas in the 1860s-1870s (not sourced here).

from.description: Shawnee settlement near Cape Girardeau, Missouri

to.description: 50 miles square west of Missouri on the Kansas River (Kansas Shawnee reserve)

removals.quote: a tract of land equal to fifty (50) miles square, situated west of the State of Missouri, and within the purchase lately made from the Osage

sources.what: Treaty of Oct. 26, 1832 (Shawnee and Delaware of Cape Girardeau)

removals.notes: Which of the three federally recognized Shawnee nations descend from this group is uncertain (Absentee and Shawnee Tribe both listed). Royce 318-320 are the Kansas tracts listed under the 1825 treaty.

removals.people: Shawnee of Wapakoneta and Hog Creek, Ohio

from.description: Wapakoneta and Hog Creek reservations, Ohio

to.description: 100,000 acres within the Shawnee tract west of Missouri (Kansas)

legal_basis.statute: Act of May 28, 1830 (Indian Removal Act), ch. 148

removals.quote: to be removed in a convenient and suitable manner to the Western side of the Mississippi river, and will grant by patent in fee simple
removals.notes: The treaty cites the Act of May 28, 1830. Royce 318-320 (Kansas Shawnee lands) tied to the 1825 treaty; link approximate.

from.description: Seneca reservation on the Sandusky River, Ohio

to.description: Tract adjoining the northern boundary of the Cherokee lands on the Neosho (Grand) River, northeastern Oklahoma

removals.quote: to be removed in a convenient and suitable manner, to the western side of the Mississippi river; and will grant them, by patent, in fee simple
removals.notes: Census code 5835 (Seneca-Cayuga OTSA) approximate; the 1831 reserve lay in what is now Ottawa and Delaware counties, Oklahoma, and was ceded back in 1867.

removals.people: Mixed Seneca and Shawnee of Lewistown, Ohio

from.description: Lewistown reservation, Logan County, Ohio

legal_basis.statute: Act of May 28, 1830 (Indian Removal Act), ch. 148

removals.quote: the United States agree to cause the said band of Senecas and Shawnees, consisting of about three hundred souls, to be removed in a convenient and suitable manner to the western side of the Mississippi river

sources.what: Treaty of Dec. 29, 1832 at the Seneca agency on the Cowskin River

removals.notes: Census 5640 (Eastern Shawnee OTSA) approximate. Lewistown, Ohio has no Wikidata item found; from.place omitted.

from.description: Delaware lands in Indiana (Treaty of St. Mary's, Oct. 3, 1818)
from.place_note: Placed by the thread session from this stage's own description (Delaware towns on the White River, Indiana; from memory)

to.description: Country west of the Mississippi; Delawares settled on the James Fork of White River, Missouri
to.place_note: Royce 150a is the Delaware land in Missouri held under the 1818 treaty and its 1829 supplement (land-cessions.json)

removals.quote: the United States agree to provide for the Delawares a country to reside in, upon the west side of the Mississippi, and to guaranty to them the peaceable possession of the same
removals.notes: Royce number for the 1818 Delaware cession not matched by treaty id in the project file; omitted. James Fork location is from the 1829 treaty recital.

from.description: James Fork of White River, Missouri; also the Delaware reserve on the Sandusky, Ohio, ceded Aug. 3, 1829

to.description: Fork of the Kansas and Missouri rivers (Delaware reserve, Wyandotte and Leavenworth counties, Kansas)

removals.quote: remove, on the following conditions, from the country on James fork of White river in the State of Missouri, to the Country selected in the fork of the Kansas and Missouri River
removals.notes: Royce 316/317 are the Kansas Delaware tracts listed under the 1854 treaty (not verified for 1829). The Delaware Nation (Anadarko) descends from groups that split off to Texas; not captured.

from.description: Delaware reserve in Kansas

to.description: Cherokee Nation lands, northeastern Indian Territory (Washington and Nowata counties, Oklahoma)

removals.quote: a tract of land ceded to the Government by the Choctaws and Chickasaws, the Creeks, or the Seminoles, or which may be ceded by the Cherokees in the Indian country
removals.notes: The 1866 treaty provides land to be bought from the Choctaw/Chickasaw, Creek, Seminole or Cherokee; the actual purchase was from the Cherokee under the 1867 agreement (not sourced). The Delaware Tribe has no census area in its yaml, so a place is given; Nowata County is an anchor.

from.description: Wyandot reservations at Upper Sandusky, Ohio, and in Michigan

to.description: Tract of 148,000 acres west of the Mississippi on Indian lands (Kansas City, Kansas, at the confluence of the Kansas and Missouri rivers, bought from the Delawares)

removals.quote: a tract of land west of the Mississippi River, to contain one hundred and forty-eight thousand acres
removals.notes: Treaty does not name Kansas; the Wyandot bought land from the Delawares in 1843 at the Kansas River mouth. Removal July 1843.

from.description: Wyandotte lands at Kansas City, Kansas

to.description: Land ceded by the Senecas, north of the Seneca reserve on the Neosho River, Indian Territory

removals.quote: The United States will set apart for the Wyandottes for their future home the land ceded by the Senecas in the first article hereof, and described in said article
removals.notes: From-royce 263 is the Wyandot Kansas tract from the 1842 treaty; the 1867 treaty itself did not cede it. Not all Wyandot moved (the Wyandot Nation of Kansas remained).

from.description: Miami lands on the Wabash in Indiana

to.description: 500,000 acres west of Missouri (Miami County, Kansas)

removals.quote: the Miami tribe of Indians shall remove to the country assigned them west of the Mississippi, within five years from this date
removals.notes: Removal enforced by U.S. troops in 1846; many Miami families with reserves stayed in Indiana. Treaty deadline was 1845. The enforcement by U.S. troops is sourced in evidence.json; about 161 Miami stayed in Indiana by treaty or joint resolution.

from.description: Miami reserve in Miami County, Kansas

to.description: Peoria reservation in the northeastern Indian Territory (Ottawa County, Oklahoma)

removals.quote: The Peorias, Kaskaskias, Weas, and Piankeshaws agree that the Miamies may be confederated with them upon their new reservation
removals.notes: The treaty only lets the Miami join the Peoria reservation; the 1873 date of the move is from history and not sourced here. From-royce 329/330 are Kansas tracts from the 1854 treaty.

removals.people: Ottawa of Blanchard's Fork and Roche de Boeuf, Ohio

from.description: Reservations at Blanchard's Fork, Little Auglaize and Roche de Boeuf, Ohio

to.description: 34,000 acres adjoining the Shawnee tract west of Missouri (Franklin County, Kansas; Ottawa reserve)

legal_basis.statute: Act of May 28, 1830 (Indian Removal Act), ch. 148

removals.quote: to be removed, in a convenient and suitable manner, to the western side of the Mississippi river; and will grant, by patent in fee simple
removals.notes: The Roche de Boeuf band did not agree to remove in 1831; they ceded in the 1833 treaty and followed later. The Franklin County anchor for the Ottawa reserve is from history, not the treaty.

removals.people: Ottawa of Blanchard's Fork and Roche de Boeuf

from.description: Ottawa reserve in Franklin County, Kansas

to.description: West part of the Shawnee reservation in Indian Territory (Ottawa County, Oklahoma)

removals.quote: The west part of the Shawnee reservation, ceded to the United States by the third article, is hereby sold to the Ottawas
removals.notes: Most Ottawa became citizens under the 1862 treaty; those who went to Indian Territory did so in the 1870s. The quote names the land purchased, not a removal order.

removals.people: Kaskaskia, Peoria, Wea and Piankashaw (Illinois Confederacy)

from.description: Illinois and Missouri lands of the Peoria and Kaskaskia; Wea and Piankashaw lands in Illinois and Missouri
from.place_note: Royce 48 and 96a are the Illinois lands of the Kaskaskia and Peoria (land-cessions.json)

to.description: 150 sections west of Missouri on the Osage River (Miami County, Kansas) plus 250 sections for the Piankashaw and Wea

removals.quote: one hundred and fifty sections of land forever, or as long as they live upon it as a tribe, to include the present Peoria village, west of the State of Missouri, on the waters of Osage river
removals.notes: Royce 326-328 are Kansas reserve tracts (destination). From-royce omitted because the Illinois cessions are older (e.g. 48, 96a in 1818). The Wea 1818 Indiana cession (Royce 74, 114) is not a separate stage. Miami listed because the 1867 treaty merged the groups.

from.description: Confederated Peoria reserve in Miami County, Kansas

to.description: Land bought from the Senecas and Quapaws south of Kansas, northeastern Indian Territory (Ottawa County, Oklahoma)

removals.quote: remove to their new homes in the Indian country within two years from the ratification of this treaty

removals.people: New York Indians (Seneca, Cayuga, Onondaga, Oneida, Tuscarora, St. Regis, Stockbridge, Munsee, Brothertown)

from.description: Reservations in western New York (Buffalo Creek, Cattaraugus, Allegany, Tonawanda) and Green Bay lands in Wisconsin

to.description: 1,824,000 acres directly west of Missouri (Kansas tract, Neosho County area)

removals.quote: the United States agree to set apart the following tract of country, situated directly west of the State of Missouri, as a permanent home for all the New York Indians
removals.notes: The treaty was obtained by fraud and bribery and was largely not carried out; about 200 Senecas went to Kansas in 1846 and many returned. The 1842 compromise restored part of the New York reservations. Kansas lands were later sold. The nation list is broad and approximate; Tonawanda signed separately in 1857.

removals.people: New York Indians (Oneida, Stockbridge, Munsee, Brothertown)

from.description: Oneida, Stockbridge and Brothertown towns in central and western New York
from.place_note: Placed by the thread session from this stage's own description (the Oneida Indian Nation's present land in New York, as an anchor for the New York towns)

to.description: Land on Fox River and the east side of Lake Winnebago, Wisconsin (Green Bay and Kaukauna area)

removals.quote: may be set apart as a home to the several tribes of the New York Indians, who may remove to, and settle upon the same, within three years from the date of this agreement
removals.notes: The migration began 1822 under Menominee-Winnebago agreements (not in Kappler, not fetched). The 1831-32 treaties confirmed the settlement. Royce 158-162 are Menominee cessions in Wisconsin, omitted as they are not the New York origin. Brothertown moved 1831-1836.

from.description: Stockbridge township on the east side of Lake Winnebago, Calumet County, Wisconsin

to.description: Reservation in Shawano County, Wisconsin

removals.quote: two townships of land on the east side of Winnebago Lake, Territory of Wisconsin
removals.notes: Quote is the origin recital (two townships on Lake Winnebago); the destination (Shawano County lands) is in the operative articles, not quoted. Royce 272 and 403 listed for WI.

from.description: Stockbridge township east of Lake Winnebago, Wisconsin

to.description: Land west of the Mississippi to be procured by the President (not located)

removals.quote: they will remove to the country set apart for them, or such other west of the Mississipi River
removals.notes: The Senate-amended treaty provided for removal west of the Mississippi; the removal was never carried out and the tribe stayed, receiving Shawano County lands in 1856.

from.description: Menominee lands in Wisconsin ceded by the 1848 treaty (Wolf River and Green Bay country)

to.description: Land on the upper Mississippi ceded by the Chippewa in 1847, on the Crow Wing River, Minnesota

removals.quote: all that country or tract of land ceded to the said United States by the Chippewa Indians of the Mississippi and Lake Superior, in the treaty of August 2, 1847

sources.what: Treaty of May 12, 1854: recites Menominee unwillingness to remove to Crow Wing and permission to stay on the Wolf and Oconto rivers

removals.notes: Removal was ordered 1850-52 but the Menominee refused; the 1854 treaty reversed it and set the Wolf River reservation. The quote does not name Crow Wing; the 1854 treaty recital does ("upon Crow Wing, which had been assigned them"). The Menominee never reached Crow Wing; the only move (Nov. 1852) was within Wisconsin.

from.description: Osage homelands in Missouri and Arkansas Territory (Osage River / Neosho valleys), ceded 1825

to.description: Osage reserve in southeastern Kansas Territory, 50 by 50 miles west of Missouri, reserved in the same treaty

removals.quote: there shall be reserved, to, and for, the Great and Little Osage Tribes or Nations, aforesaid, so long as they may choose to occupy the same, the following described tract of land

sources.what: Kappler text of Treaty with the Osage, June 2, 1825

removals.notes: Cession of Missouri/Arkansas land with a reserved Kansas tract; treaty-based relocation, not an escorted removal. Earlier cessions (1808 Fort Osage, Royce 67-69; 1818, Royce 97) not given separate stages because the treaties do not direct a move. Royce 123 matched by treaty; 475 is the Kansas reserve (also 1865).

from.description: Osage diminished reserve in southeastern Kansas (Drum Creek / Neosho)
